articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5, featuring significantly improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation within a single model, and a vastly expanded context window. The model demonstrates substantial gains on graduate-level science benchmarks and complex multi-step coding tasks, marking a notable jump in unified multimodal capability over GPT-4o.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra Achieves New State-of-the-Art on Agentic Coding Benchmarks
articles.summary: DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Ultra with a focus on autonomous software engineering tasks, reporting top scores on SWE-Bench Verified and a new internal multi-repo refactoring benchmark. The model can sustain coherent plans across hundreds of files and execute multi-step tool use chains, intensifying the race for AI-driven software development agents.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoids in BMW Factories
articles.summary: Figure announced that its third-generation humanoid robot, Figure 03, has entered full commercial deployment at two BMW manufacturing facilities in South Carolina. The robots handle parts kitting, inspection, and bin-picking tasks autonomously for full 8-hour shifts, representing one of the first scaled commercial humanoid deployments in automotive manufacturing.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Dexterous Manipulation and Unsupervised Task Learning
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its latest Optimus Gen 3 prototype performing complex dexterous manipulation tasks including cable routing and small-object assembly, learned primarily through vision-based imitation learning with minimal human demonstration. The company announced plans to deploy several thousand units internally by end of 2026, claiming unit production costs are approaching $25,000.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude Sonnet 4 with Verified Reasoning Traces and Improved Instruction Following
articles.summary: Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 4, featuring cryptographically verifiable reasoning traces that allow enterprises to audit the model's chain-of-thought for compliance and safety. The model shows marked improvement in following complex, multi-constraint system prompts and reduced sycophancy, addressing key enterprise adoption concerns around reliability and auditability.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of A14 2nm Node, Enabling Next-Generation AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed that risk production on its N2 (2nm) process using gate-all-around transistor architecture has commenced, with initial wafers earmarked for Apple and NVIDIA AI accelerator designs. The node promises up to 25% performance gains at equivalent power or 30% power reduction at equivalent performance, critical for the next wave of data center and edge AI chips.

articles.title: Microsoft and Atom Computing Demonstrate Logical Qubit Error Correction Below Fault-Tolerance Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Atom Computing jointly announced achieving sustained logical qubit error rates below the fault-tolerance threshold using a neutral-atom quantum processor with 256 physical qubits. This milestone, verified by independent teams, brings practical fault-tolerant quantum computation closer and validates the neutral-atom approach as competitive with superconducting and trapped-ion architectures.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Begins: First Wave of High-Risk AI System Compliance Audits Launched
articles.summary: The European Union commenced its first formal compliance audits under the AI Act, targeting high-risk AI systems in hiring, credit scoring, and critical infrastructure. Several major US tech companies face scrutiny over transparency and bias documentation requirements, setting early precedents for how the landmark regulation will be enforced in practice across global AI deployments.
